method: Independent exact-file review with original pixels, matched cameras, checked hashes, primary-source comparison and scoped runtime evidence. See observations and evidence inventory.
observations: Independently opened NPS Geodiversity Atlas Arches page, Arch Formation and Geologic Features/Processes, and NPS Geologic Formations, A Story in Stone / Why So Many Arches. References were consulted for broad jointed sandstone, partings and differential erosion, not copied media.

The asset has a real through-opening and two-sided closed rock volume. Independently decoded triangles have 1,347 welded edges each incident to two triangles, zero positional boundary edges and single-sided materials. Overall depth is 2.107665 m; sampled central upper-rock front/back vertex extent is about 1.078079 m. The latter is an extent observation, not a minimum-thickness guarantee.

The narrow side silhouette is consistent with a stylized rock fin and is supported by sideclay, top, reversehero and orbit pixels. No unsupported need for extra ornament or uniformly thick torus geometry was imposed.

Claim scope is evidence-informed, time-neutral sandstone concept. Exact outline, scale, colors and bed placement are artistic choices. Neither named-site identity, ancient environmental reconstruction, formation age nor engineering stability is certified. NPS geological time context does not make a modern arch a Jurassic landscape.
limitations: No self-intersection or geotechnical engineering certification.
No reference photos or text incorporated into asset.
